prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1003; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss for side impact collision at signalized intersection. Insured reports other vehicle entered intersection against the red signal and struck driver's side door. Police report requested. Insured reports neck and back discomfort at scene, declined ambulance transport.

Entry 2: Contacted claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation. Attorney advised all communication should route through their office going forward. Requested medical authorization forms and prior treatment history for neck and lower back. Photos of both vehicles requested from insured and claimant.

Entry 3: Reviewed police report. Responding officer cited other driver for failure to obey traffic control device. Independent witness statement obtained confirming signal color. Liability assessment leaning strongly toward other driver. Injury claim to be evaluated against medical records once received.

Entry 4: Received initial treatment records from claimant's provider showing cervical and lumbar strain diagnosis, muscle relaxants and physical therapy referral. No fractures or imaging abnormalities noted. Records forwarded to medical review for evaluation of treatment duration and necessity.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding status. Attorney indicated demand package will follow after treatment concludes. Reserve reviewed and adjusted to reflect current injury severity and liability position. File remains open pending completion of medical treatment and receipt of demand.
